title: Queue Lighthouse — weekly reflection
content:
Purpose: quick weekly reflection from the Queue Lighthouse sync (30m) — focus on queue rebalancer experiments, KV shadowing errors observed in Canary-2, and microbatching fairness tweaks.

Attendees: Samira (notes), Ethan, Priya, Rafael, Jun, + on-call rotation ping (Maya).

Summary (tl;dr):
- Rebalancer hypothesis seems promising: fewer long-tail latency spikes when we bias sampling by idle-slot-age. 5% drop in 99th p50->p99 tail during a controlled synthetic workload.
- Canary-2 showed sporadic KV shadow misses when prefill window overlapped with eviction job A. Root cause likely race in prefill commit path + async eviction marker.
- Microbatch fairness change (soft cap per origin) reduced starvation for low-QPS tenants but introduced extra scheduling churn at high QPS — need hybrid threshold.

Notes / observations:
1) Rebalancer experiment (ethan):
   - Setup: 8-node runner with synthetic mix (short chat + long generation). Enabled age-biased sampler (weight = 1 + age_secs/30 clipped).
   - Result: mean latency unchanged, p99 reduced from 820ms -> 780ms; p995 down ~6%. Throughput stable.
   - Side effects: slightly larger variance in batch sizes for very low-QPS classes.
   - Action: roll rebalancer to perf-lab for 48h and monitor median batch-size per origin. Test metric: origin_batch_var <= 1.5x baseline.

2) KV shadowing & prefill race (priya + jun):
   - Symptom: Canary-2 traces show prefill returning empty KV state for some requests that immediately follow eviction markers. Observed ~0.02% of requests.
   - Hypothesis: eviction job emits marker then async cleanup removes slots before prefill commit completes; prefill path checks marker but does not wait for in-flight commit; commit may be queued behind GC.
   - Quick mitigation: add a short (50ms) jittered backoff when prefill sees recent eviction marker before treating as miss.
   - Long term fix: strengthen commit ordering in allocator (ensure commit write is persisted before marker propagated), or change eviction to tombstone then GC sweep after grace window.
   - Action items: Priya to prototype marker->commit barrier (INF-2410). Jun to run stress with synthetic eviction bursts and measure miss rate.

3) Microbatching fairness (rafael):
   - Change: introduced soft per-tenant cap on microbatch size (soft_cap = max(8, mean_batch * 0.7)). Low-QPS tenants improved latency.
   - Problem: under flash crowd the scheduler attempts to enforce soft caps leading to extra requeueing and CPU overhead; also increases reorderer churn.
   - Idea: add an adaptive fallback that disables soft caps when global CPU util > 85% for > 5s.
   - Action: Rafael to add adaptive switch and benchmark with 10k tenant mix. ETA 1 sprint.

4) Thermal/infra & kernel tuning (jun):
   - Kernel patch v3 (jit scheduling tweak) rolled to staging: small perf wins (~2%). But tests showed one platform (p4-large) with thermal throttle under repeated long-generation tests.
   - Note: thermal events correlate with large contiguous batches; consider jittering batch alignment to spread GPU load.
   - Action: Jun to add thermal probe in perf lab that disables big-batches when GPU temp > 78C; also add telemetry tag for batch alignment.

Runbook / Oncall notes:
- If KV miss rate > 0.1% sustained for 10min, escalate to eng-serving-runtime and flip prefill backoff flag. (oncall checklist updated).
- If scheduler churn causes CPU steal > 20% alert SRE with "queue-lighthouse-scheduler" tag.

Open questions / unresolved:
- What is the root latency cost of the marker->commit barrier? If we force linear writes we might regress median latency for small requests. Need microbench.
- How aggressive should soft caps be for PLG customers vs enterprise tenants? Should be config-driven per-tenant tier.
- Do we accept slightly larger batch variance for improved p99? Agree threshold: p99 improvement must be >= 3% without >10% increase in p50.

Decisions made this week:
- Approve 48h rebalancer stress on perf-lab. Owner: Ethan. Gate: no regression in throughput and p50 < +5%.
- Enable 50ms prefill backoff on Canary-2 as temporary mitigation. Owner: Priya. Rollback plan: remove flag if latency regresses within 2h.
- Add adaptive soft-cap disable when CPU>85%. Owner: Rafael.

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Ethan: run rebalancer perf-lab run, collect origin_batch_var, p99, p995 - ETA: 2026-01-14.
- Priya: prototype commit->marker barrier and temp backoff flag for Canary-2 - ETA: prototype 2026-01-20, backoff live 2026-01-12.
- Jun: thermal probe + batch-alignment telemetry in perf lab - ETA: 2026-01-18.
- Rafael: adaptive soft-cap toggle and 10k tenant benchmark - ETA: 2026-01-25.
- Samira: update oncall runbook doc with new thresholds and post link to team slack - ETA: 2026-01-12.

Notes-to-self / scribbles (rough):
- try combining age-bias with small dampening factor so tiny origins don't get too many splits.
- test marker->commit ordering with accelerated GC simulated (lower grace window).
- chat with infra about thermal mitigation options at hardware level (fan policy?)

Meeting artifacts: attached traces saved to perf-lab bucket and linked in JIRA INF-2384. Recording: internal-call/2026-01-11/queue-lighthouse.mp4 (private).

End of reflection. Short, actionable, keep moving.

Edited 2026-01-12: added microbatch adaptive idea after Rafael's afternoon run, clarified Canary mitigation timeline.
